title: Analysis of Decreased Employment in Permanent Jobs for Fresh Graduates in Past Two Years and Measures to Monitor and Boost Employment
what_it_is: Analysis of Decreased Employment in Permanent Jobs for Fresh Graduates in Past Two Years and Measures to Monitor and Boost Employment

sections.label: Graduate employment survey questions
sections.summary: Questions ask the Minister for Education about factors behind lower graduate employment, sector variation, rising median salaries, and monitoring of higher fresh graduate unemployment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education in view of the 2024 Joint Autonomous Universities Graduate Employment Survey which showed that salaries were higher but fewer graduates found employment within six months of completing their final exams (a) what factors are contributing to the decrease in the employment rate; (b) how do the fresh graduate employment rates vary across sectors; and (c) what is driving the increase in median salary among fresh graduates despite fewer jobs on offer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education in respect of the Joint Autonomous Universities Graduate Employment Survey 2024, what is the Ministry doing to monitor, manage and mitigate the higher unemployment rate of fresh graduates as compared to the past two years.

sections.label: Rising fresh graduate salaries
sections.summary: Median salaries for fresh graduates rose 4.2% year-on-year in 2024, even as the total number of fresh AU graduates increased over five years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: Median salaries for fresh graduates have also continued to rise, with a year-on-year increase of 4.2% in 2024, even as the total number of fresh AU graduates increased over the past five years.

sections.label: Employment below pre-COVID levels
sections.summary: The full-time employment rate for fresh graduates regressed to pre-COVID levels in 2023 and fell below them in 2024, significantly so in certain sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: But this regressed back to pre-COVID levels in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: And then in 2024, the full-time employment rate for fresh graduates has actually come in below pre-COVID levels, and quite significantly so for certain sectors.

sections.label: Full-time employment rate
sections.summary: In 2024, about 95% of this age group were in full-time employment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: In 2024, about 95% of this age group were in full-time employment.

sections.label: Reviewing university places
sections.summary: MOE regularly reviews sector investment forecasts with MTI and MOM and adjusts university places for each course to equip graduates with needed skills.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: On the second question, to ensure that our graduates are equipped with skills that are needed to access good employment opportunities, MOE regularly reviews together with the Ministry of Trade and Industry, and the Ministry of Manpower the forecasts of sectors' investments and from there, adjusts the university places for each course.

sections.label: Higher median salary drivers
sections.summary: The higher median salary reflects market trends and more graduates being drawn to growth sectors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: The higher median salary that we are seeing reflects the market trends and also how more of our graduates are being drawn to the growth sectors.

sections.label: Graduate Employment Survey six-month snapshot
sections.summary: The Graduate Employment Survey gives a six-month snapshot, and about half of unemployed respondents had job offers, most starting work later.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: Also, in my earlier point, in response to Mr Xie Yao Quan's question, the Graduate Employment Survey just gives us a snapshot at the six-month mark.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: We do know that amongst those who responded that they were unemployed after six months of graduation, actually, about half of them had received job offers, and about I think two-thirds of this group that received job offers that had still not yet started work, they were going to start work in due course.

sections.label: Post-COVID ICT demand and salaries
sections.summary: Post-COVID, demand for ICT workers surged and starting salaries for graduates in the sector spiked.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: Post-COVID, we saw a sudden surge in demand for workers in ICT and also a spike in the starting salary for graduates in this sector.

sections.label: Enough jobs and employment rates
sections.summary: There are enough jobs in the economy, and full-time employment rates for employed graduates aged 25 to 29 remain about 95%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: There are enough jobs though in our economy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: And as you can see, the full-time employment rates of our employed graduates in the 25 to 29 age group remains decently high – about 95%, if I recall correctly.

sections.label: Course cluster employment rate drops
sections.summary: From 2022 to 2024, Art, Design and Media fell 11.3% to 60.9% and Engineering fell 12.3% to 79.3%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: With reference to the Graduate Employment Survey, if we look at course clusters such as Art, Design and Media, post-COVID, 2022 to 2024, Art, Design and Media, a 11.3% drop to 60.9%; Engineering was 91.6%, dropped to 79.3%, and that is a 12.3% drop; and so forth.

sections.label: Review curriculum for adjacent competencies
sections.summary: A member asks whether MOE will review course curriculum and structure to develop adjacent competencies more structurally.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But the second point he made also was about developing adjacent competencies for these graduates, and this includes those university graduates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, my point is, can we foresee at the MOE level for there to be a review of course curriculum, course structure to develop these adjacent competencies in a more structured and directed manner?

sections.label: Survey snapshot and adult employment
sections.summary: The Graduate Employment Survey is a six-month snapshot; for Singaporean adults aged 25 to 29, employment is 95% and long-term unemployment very low.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: The Graduate Employment Survey is just a snapshot of the employment situation at the six-month mark after graduation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: I think it is important for us to take a step back and look at the employment of our Singaporean adults in the age group, say 25 to 29.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: The employment rate is 95% and the long-term unemployment for this group is very low.

sections.label: Graduate employment beyond six months
sections.summary: The speaker says graduates' employment is looked at beyond the last three years and beyond six months after graduation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: I have also replied that for our university graduates, we look beyond the last three years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: And I think it is important that we not just look at a longer timeframe to ascertain the trend and whether there is some intervention that we require, but also look at beyond the six-month mark.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: So, beyond six months after graduation, what is the employment and employability of our graduates?

sections.label: Skills for good jobs
sections.summary: The speaker says what matters most is that graduates have the required skills to get good jobs with good starting pay and trajectory.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: What matters most, whether is it their graduates from our universities or polytechnics, is that they have the required skills to get good jobs, not just at the starting, with good starting pay, but with good trajectory.

sections.label: Long-term course design for skills
sections.summary: The speaker says courses must be designed with a long-term view of market skill sets and adjacent skills for future jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: It takes us four years to produce a graduate.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: So, when we design our courses, we must have a long-term perspective of what are the skill sets that are required by the market, not in the next one to two years, but in the next five to 10 years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: And more importantly, what are the adjacent skill sets that will allow our people to pivot to new jobs that may be created and may not be even in existence today.
